units.text: INT. HARBORVIEW VETERINARY CLINIC - NIGHT
Every war leaves a trail of paperwork. Nobody tells you the paperwork is the part that gets people killed.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Fluorescent tubes buzz over a waiting room that smells of bleach and wet dog, and Detective Mara Ruiz, fifties, rain on her shoulders, stands at the reception desk with a manila folder pressed to her chest while Dr. Femi Okafor, forties, blood on his scrubs, pulls a shutter down over the front window, and behind them four uniformed soldiers in damp fatigues fan out through the kennel hall, boots squeaking on the linoleum, rifles low, checking cages full of sleeping beagles and one furious cat.
Three tours, one medal, and now a vet clinic at two in the morning. That's how it ends for the kind of man we came to find.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Hall's clear!
units.name: THE SQUAD

units.text: Dr. Okafor, I'm going to ask you once.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: You have been asking since you walked in.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: Where is Sergeant Hale?
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Sedated. Surgery two. He walked in with a shrapnel wound and a dog that was bleeding worse than he was.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: A dog.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: A Belgian Malinois. Military issue, tag filed off. I stitched the dog first. The man made me.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: And you didn't think to call anyone.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: I thought a dying animal outranked a phone call. Was I wrong?
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: You're harboring a deserter who is wanted in connection with eleven deaths.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: I'm harboring a patient. He has a pulse. That's all my license asks me to check.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: Your license is going to be the least of your problems.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Then arrest me after he wakes up. I'd like him to wake up.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: You think he's innocent.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: I think he talks in his sleep. Under anesthesia he kept saying the same name, over and over, and it wasn't a woman's name and it wasn't a place.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: Whose name?
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Yours.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: There it was. Twenty years of keeping my past in a locked drawer, and a veterinarian hands me the key.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: He's lying to you.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Sedatives don't let you lie, Detective. That's rather the point of them.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: Detective, we have movement in surgery two!
units.name: THE SQUAD

units.text: Nobody touches that door until I say.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: He'll tear his sutures if he stands.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: Then he should have thought about that before he ran.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Ran from what? Tell me that much. Tell me what a man like that runs from.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: From me.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Silence.
The cat hisses.

Somewhere in the back, a steel tray CLATTERS to the floor, and Ruiz, hand on her holster, shoulders through the swinging doors as the Squad closes in behind her, lamps swinging across the kennels, Okafor following with his palms raised, and on the operating table the blanket lies empty, the window above it open to the rain, the Malinois sitting upright beneath it, waiting, staring at her as if it had been told she would come.
He didn't run from me. He ran to me. The dog was the message. The dog was always the message.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: What does that mean?
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: It means we are standing in exactly the place he wanted us to be.
units.name: RUIZ

units.text: Contact! Front entrance!
units.name: THE SQUAD

units.text: The lights die.
Rain.
Boots.
Dark.
